Good morning. Cloud storage misconfiguration remains the number one source of data breaches worldwide. Traditional tools either rely on naive string matching that floods security teams with false alarms, or are tested on toy 4-file samples. In this capstone, we built a condition-aware policy evaluation engine, validated it against a 120-policy ground-truth benchmark dataset, and demonstrated high-precision detection with automated remediation.
//THREAT MODEL & DETECTION TARGETS

What the Scanner Has to Catch: Beyond Naive Checks

Four core breach vectors mapped directly to CIS AWS Foundations v3.0 & documented real-world incidents

01
CIS 2.1.1 Public Access & Unauthenticated Reads

Buckets or objects readable by the public or "Principal": "*". Documented in breaches like the Deep Root Analytics 198M voter records leak.

"Principal": "*" → Evaluates missing IP / VPC condition blocks
02
CIS 1.16 Excessive IAM Actions & Wildcards

Wildcard permissions (s3:*, s3:Get*) granting full data exfiltration & bucket deletion. Exploited in SSRF-to-IAM credential theft (e.g. Capital One).

"Action": "s3:*" → Flags wildcard over-privilege across roles
03
CIS 2.1.2 & 2.1.3 Transport & At-Rest Gaps

Unencrypted buckets (no SSE-KMS) and unforced HTTP traffic. Adversaries intercepting plaintext transfers or accessing raw unencrypted storage snapshots.

aws:SecureTransport != true → Detects absence of TLS Deny
04
CIS 2.1.4 & 2.1.5 Auditability & Tamper Resistance

Missing access logging and object versioning. In a ransomware attack, attackers overwrite or delete backups with zero forensic trail remaining for response teams.

Logging: disabled | ObjectLock: off → Flags forensic blindness
▸ real attacks exploit subtle multi-statement gaps, not just plain single lines
Page 2 / 7
Most student projects look for simple keywords. But cloud breaches don't happen because someone forgot how to type JSON; they happen because multi-statement interactions leave dangerous loopholes. We cover the four core pillars: unauthenticated public exposure, excessive wildcard privileges, transport and encryption gaps, and forensic audit blindness.

★ Key Technical Advancement: Solving The AWS IAM Evaluation Logic
1. Explicit Deny Precedence: In AWS, an explicit Deny always overrides an Allow. Naive scanners see "Principal": "*" and immediately report a false positive even if a companion statement contains a strict Deny condition for external traffic.
2. Condition Key Resolution: Our parser parses aws:SourceIp, aws:PrincipalOrgID, and aws:SecureTransport. This differentiates actual public exposure from corporate-authorized external access.
▸ architectural soundness prevents the alert fatigue that causes teams to ignore security tools
Page 3 / 7
Here is our architecture. The key innovation in Stage 3 is our IAM and Condition Engine. In AWS, policy evaluation isn't linear: an explicit Deny overrides an Allow, and condition keys like aws:SourceIp can restrict an otherwise open wildcard. By normalizing the AST and modeling AWS evaluation semantics, we eliminate false alarms that naive regex scanners produce.

The Evaluation Dataset: Ground Truth vs Toy Tests

Directly addressing rigorous evaluation: 120 labeled AWS policy configurations with known ground-truth matrix

Dataset Category Count Description / Breach Pattern Ground Truth Label
Clear-Cut Vulnerabilities 40 files Unrestricted public read/write, wildcard IAM admin, disabled encryption Vulnerable (Positive)
Condition-Restricted (Tricky Safe) 30 files Wildcard Principal restricted via IP CIDR, VPC Endpoint, or OrgID Safe (Negative)
Subtle Bypasses (Tricky Bad) 30 files Incomplete TLS Deny, partial wildcards (s3:Get*), cross-account trusts Vulnerable (Positive)
CIS-Hardened Baselines 20 files Full production hardening: KMS CMK, TLS 1.3 enforced, Object Lock Safe (Negative)
Total Corpus: 120 labeled policies • Labeled matrix in dataset/ground_truth.json with exact expected CIS rule violation IDs.
✗ Why 4 Toy Files Failed Evaluation

Hand-crafting 3 bad files and 1 good file to test a scanner is a unit test, not an evaluation. It cannot test false positive resistance or condition parsing.

✓ How Our 120-Policy Suite Fixes It

Includes 60 adversarial trap policies designed specifically to trip scanners into false alarms or missed detections. Every result is mathematically verified.

▸ testing on a labeled dataset is what separates an academic research project from a script

This slide directly addresses the professor's feedback. Rather than testing on 4 toy files, we created 'CloudSec-S3-Bench-120'—a standardized benchmark of 120 ground-truth labeled policies. Crucially, half the dataset contains tricky edge cases: policies that look vulnerable but are actually secured by conditions (testing for false positives), and policies that look harmless but contain bypasses (testing for false negatives).

Here are our empirical results. Against the 120 benchmark policies, a naive regex scanner achieves an intolerable 48% false positive rate because it flags every wildcard without inspecting conditions. Our engine achieves 97.1% Precision and Recall, with an FPR of only 4.0%. In terms of throughput, it processes over 1,200 policies per second, proving it can easily run in real-time CI/CD pipelines.
//DEVSECOPS INTEGRATION

Closing the Loop: Automated Remediation

Shifting from passive alert reporting to actionable, automated fix generation in CI/CD pipelines

[!] DETECTED VULNERABILITY (CIS 2.1.3)

Missing TLS Transport Enforcement

Target bucket s3://finance-records-2025 allows plaintext HTTP access. Plaintext transmission exposes banking records to on-path interception.

Severity: HIGH (CVSS 7.5) • Rule: cis_2_1_3_tls_enforce
remediation — terraform-patch.tf
# Automated Remediation generated by CloudSec Scanner
resource "aws_s3_bucket_policy" "enforce_tls" {
bucket = aws_s3_bucket.finance_records.id
policy = jsonencode({
Version = "2012-10-17"
Statement = [{
Sid = "EnforceTLSRequestsOnly"
Effect = "Deny"
Principal = "*"
Action = "s3:*"
Resource = "${aws_s3_bucket.finance_records.arn}/*"
Condition = { Bool = { "aws:SecureTransport" = "false" } }
}]
})
}

# Equivalent AWS CLI instant hotfix:
$ aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket finance-records --policy file://fix.json
▸ actionable fixes turn security from a roadblock into an automated enabler
Page 6 / 7
Security tools that only output error messages fail in real organizations because developers don't know how to fix them. Our scanner closes the loop: whenever a finding is triggered, it compiles the exact Terraform block or AWS CLI command needed to remediate the vulnerability. Developers can apply the fix with a single click.
